Measure the provisional 100 μM Disaccharides Solutions for UV absorption at 232 nm Here, a Molecular Devices SpectraMax i3x Multi-Mode Plate Reader (Softmax Pro 7.1.2) was used to measure UV absorption at 232 nM: Add 200 μL of each 100 μM Disaccharide Solution to individual wells of a UV-transparent 96 well plate, in triplicate (within the software assign the wells as unknowns) To a separate well, add 200 μL ddH 2 O as a blank (within the software assign the wells as blanks) Measure the UV absorption at 232 nM For each disaccharide, average the UV absorbance values across the triplicate measurements Recover the Disaccharide Solutions and freeze at -20oC for future use UV-STAR® MICROPLATE, 96 WELL, COC, F-BOTTOM (96 well plate, Greiner, 655801, https://shop.gbo.com/en/england/products/bioscience/microplates/uv-star-microplates/96-well-uv-star-microplate/655801.html )
Sum the volumes of all Disaccharide Stocks

steps.title: Reconstitute lyophilised standards
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL ddH₂O to each vial of lyophilised disaccharide standard (0.5 mg or 1 mg) to obtain provisional stock concentrations of 0.5–1 mg mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Aliquot and store stocks
steps.instruction: Aliquot each provisional stock into suitable tubes and store at –20 °C; avoid repeat freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Calculate provisional molarity
steps.instruction: Convert each provisional concentration (mg mL⁻¹) to provisional molarity (mM) using M = C(mg mL⁻¹) / MW(g mol⁻¹). Example: HD001 (665 g mol⁻¹, 1 mg mL⁻¹) → 1.504 mM; HD002 (563 g mol⁻¹) → 1.776 mM; HD003 (605 g mol⁻¹) → 1.653 mM; HD004 (563 g mol⁻¹) → 1.776 mM; HD005 (461 g mol⁻¹) → 2.169 mM; HD006 (401 g mol⁻¹) → 2.494 mM; HD007 (503 g mol⁻¹) → 1.988 mM; HD008 (503 g mol⁻¹) → 1.988 mM; CD001 (401 g mol⁻¹) → 2.494 mM; CD002 (503 g mol⁻¹) → 1.988 mM; CD003 (503 g mol⁻¹) → 1.988 mM; CD004 (605 g mol⁻¹, 0.5 mg) → 0.826 mM; CD005 (605 g mol⁻¹, 0.5 mg) → 0.826 mM; CD006 (605 g mol⁻¹, 0.5 mg) → 0.826 mM; CD008 (503 g mol⁻¹, 0.5 mg) → 0.994 mM; HA02 (401 g mol⁻¹) → 2.494 mM.

steps.title: Vortex provisional stocks
steps.instruction: Mix each provisional stock briefly by vortexing.

steps.title: Determine UV correction factors
steps.instruction: Measure absorbance at 232 nm for each stock. Choose reference disaccharide (HD002 for HS, CD001 for CS/DS/HA). Compute correction factor = absorbance_i / absorbance_ref. Multiply provisional molarity by correction factor to obtain UV‑corrected molarity. Example HS corrected concentrations: HD001 3.976 mM (factor 2.644), HD002 1.776 mM (factor 1.000), HD003 1.685 mM (factor 1.019), HD004 1.991 mM (factor 1.121), HD005 1.958 mM (factor 0.902), HD006 4.021 mM (factor 1.612), HD007 1.785 mM (factor 0.898), HD008 1.797 mM (factor 0.904). Example CS/DS/HA corrected concentrations: CD001 2.494 mM (factor 1.000), CD002 2.829 mM (factor 1.423), CD003 2.143 mM (factor 1.078), CD004 0.658 mM (factor 0.797), CD005 0.569 mM (factor 0.689), CD006 0.815 mM (factor 0.986), CD008 0.690 mM (factor 0.694), HA02 1.448 mM (factor 0.581).

steps.title: Prepare CS/DS/HA equimolar mix
steps.instruction: Calculate volume V₁ for each CS/DS/HA stock needed to reach 100 µM in a final volume of 100 µL using V₁ = (C₂·V₂)/C₁ (C₂ = 0.1 mM, V₂ = 100 µL). Example volumes: CD001 4.0 µL, CD002 3.5 µL, CD003 4.7 µL, CD004 15.2 µL, CD005 17.6 µL, CD006 12.3 µL, CD008 14.5 µL, HA02 6.9 µL (total stock volume = 78.6 µL). Add the calculated volumes to a micro‑fuge tube, add ddH₂O to bring total volume to 100 µL (21.4 µL water in example), vortex briefly, and store at 4 °C for ~1 month (aliquots may be stored at –20 °C for up to 6 months; avoid repeat freeze‑thaw cycles).

substeps.instruction: Calculate V₁ for each component using V₁ = (0.1 mM × 100 µL) / C₁ (UV‑corrected concentration).
Pipette the calculated volumes into a single tube.
Add ddH₂O to reach 100 µL total volume.
Store at 4 °C (or aliquot and store at –20 °C).

steps.title: Prepare HS equimolar mix
steps.instruction: Using the HS UV‑corrected concentrations, calculate V₁ for each HS stock to obtain 100 µM in 100 µL (C₂ = 0.1 mM, V₂ = 100 µL). Example volumes: HD001 2.5 µL, HD002 5.6 µL, HD003 5.9 µL, HD004 5.0 µL, HD005 5.1 µL, HD006 2.5 µL, HD007 5.6 µL, HD008 5.6 µL (total stock volume = 37.9 µL). Add the volumes to a tube, add ddH₂O to reach 100 µL total (61.2 µL water), vortex, and store at 4 °C for ~1 month (aliquots may be stored at –20 °C for up to 6 months; avoid repeat freeze‑thaw cycles).

substeps.instruction: Calculate V₁ for each HS component using V₁ = (0.1 mM × 100 µL) / C₁.
Pipette the calculated volumes into a single tube.
Add ddH₂O to bring volume to 100 µL.
Store at 4 °C (or aliquot and store at –20 °C).

steps.title: Create dilution series
steps.instruction: Prepare dilutions of the 100 µM equimolar stock as follows: for 10 µM, add 10 µL of 100 µM stock to 90 µL ddH₂O; for 1 µM, add 10 µL of the 10 µM dilution to 90 µL ddH₂O; for 0.1 µM, add 10 µL of the 1 µM dilution to 90 µL ddH₂O. Label each micro‑fuge tube according to the target concentration, add the indicated volumes, mix well.

substeps.instruction: Add the specified volume of the higher‑concentration stock.
Add ddH₂O to reach 100 µL total volume.

description: Rationale for measurement of UV absorption of disaccharides Measurement of freshly prepared Disaccharide Stocks by UV absorption at 232 nm provides the means to normalise Disaccharide Stock concentrations, and ultimately generate mixtures of disaccharide standards at equal molar concentration (Equimolar Stock Solution). This was found to be necessary based on the observation that multiple lyophilised vials of the same disaccharide standard, after reconstitution, were found to contain differing concentrations of material (based on UV and MS responses). Here, each Disaccharide Stock is prepared to a provisional molar concentration and analysed by UV absorbance at 232 nm. Correction factors are then calculated by dividing the UV absorbance of each standard by the UV absorbance obtained from the HD002 (HS) or CD001 (CS/DS/HA). HD002 and CD001 were selected as the reference standards due to their consistency in an initial multi-batch comparison. The correction factors are used to determine the UV-corrected molar concentration of the Disaccharide Stocks. In steps 10 onwards the Disaccharide Stocks are diluted (based on their UV-corrected molar concentrations) to generate the Equimolar Stock Solution (a mixture of disaccharides at equal molar concentration, defined by their UV absorption at 232 nm)
